title: How Java achieves polymorphism
answer: Java supports compile-time polymorphism through method overloading and runtime polymorphism through method overriding and dynamic dispatch. Interfaces and superclass references provide common types that can refer to different implementations. AeroTopo's `Product` abstraction with `Orthomosaic` and `Dem` demonstrates runtime polymorphism through `resolutionMetres()`, while `LanguageLab.join` separately demonstrates compile-time overload selection.
